chunks: 1318 - Al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān al-Naysābūrī, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned in al-ʿIlal what he heard from al-Riḍā عليه السلام:

Indeed, salat was only shortened during travel because the obligatory salat as first prescribed was only ten rakʿahs, and the seven were only added to it afterward. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, lightened that addition from the servant due to the circumstance of his travel, his fatigue, his hardship, his preoccupation with his own affairs, his departure and his stay, so that he would not be distracted from what is indispensable of his livelihood, as a mercy from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and out of compassion for him—except for Salat al-Maghrib, for it is not shortened because it is a prayer shortened in its original form.

And shortening only became obligatory for eight farsakhs, no less than that and no more, because eight farsakhs is the distance of a day’s travel for ordinary people, caravans, and loaded transports. So shortening became obligatory in a day’s travel. And if it had not been obligatory in a day’s travel, it would not have been obligatory in the travel of a thousand years; because every day that comes after this day is only the counterpart of this day. So if it were not obligatory in this day, it would not be obligatory in its counterpart, since its counterpart is like it, with no difference between them.

And the voluntary prayers of the day were only omitted, while the voluntary prayers of the night were not omitted, because every prayer in which there is no shortening, there is no shortening in its voluntary prayer. That is because al-Maghrib is not shortened, so there is no shortening in the voluntary prayer after it. Likewise, al-Ghadat is not shortened, so there is no shortening in the voluntary prayer before it.

And al-ʿAtamah only became shortened, yet its two rakʿahs are not abandoned, because the two rakʿahs are not from the fifty; rather, they are an addition to the fifty as voluntary prayer, so that by means of them there may be completed, in place of each rakʿah of the obligation, two rakʿahs of voluntary prayer.

And it is only permitted for the traveler and the sick person to perform Salat al-Layl at the beginning of the night due to his preoccupation and weakness, and so that he may secure his prayer; then the sick person may rest at the time of his rest, and the traveler may attend to his engagements, his departure, and his travel.

key_terms.تَطَوُّعُ ٱلنَّهَارِ: the daytime supererogatory prayers that are omitted during travel
key_terms.ثَمَانِيَةِ فَرَاسِخَ: eight farsakhs, the travel distance that establishes the ruling
key_terms.صَلَاةَ ٱللَّيْلِ: the night prayer, which the traveler and sick person may perform earlier
key_terms.ٱلتَّقْصِيرُ: shortening the prayer from its complete form
key_terms.ٱلسَّفَرِ: travel, the state in which shortening of prayer applies
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاةَ: the ritual prayer being discussed in its obligatory and voluntary forms
key_terms.ٱلْعَتَمَةُ: the ʿIsha prayer, discussed here in relation to shortening
key_terms.ٱلْمَغْرِبِ: the sunset prayer, which is not shortened in travel

ai.seo_question: Why are prayers shortened during travel, and why is Maghrib not shortened?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the rationale for shortening salat during travel, grounding it in divine mercy and the original structure of the prescribed prayers. It also clarifies the legal distance for qaṣr, the treatment of voluntary prayers during travel, and the concession given to the traveler and the sick person regarding Salat al-Layl.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1318 - Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan al-Naysaburi, may Allah (swt) have mercy on him, mentioned among the reasons he heard from al-Ridha (as) regarding why prayers are shortened during travel.

He (Imam (as)) said: "The initially prescribed obligatory prayer was ten rak'ahs. The seven additional rak'ahs were later added, and Allah (swt), the Blessed and Exalted, lightened this addition for the servant due to the burden, fatigue, and preoccupation of travel. This relief was granted so that the servant would not become distracted from the essential needs of their livelihood during travel. However, the Maghrib prayer is not shortened because it was originally set as a shortened prayer.

The obligation to shorten applies to eight farsakhs (a day's journey) and no less. The reason for this is that eight farsakhs is a day’s journey for the common people, caravans, and baggage carriers, necessitating shortening for such a journey.
If the obligation were not established for a day’s journey, it would not be required for a journey of a thousand years, as every day after this day is similar to it ; if it were not obligatory for this day, it would not be obligatory for its equivalent.

Voluntary prayers during the day are omitted while traveling, but not voluntary prayers at night, because every prayer that is not shortened also maintains its voluntary aspect. Thus, the Maghrib prayer is not shortened, so neither are the voluntary prayers that follow it.
Similarly, the Fajr prayer is not shortened, so neither are the voluntary prayers preceding it.

The Isha prayer (Atamah) is considered shortened, but its two rak'ahs are not omitted because they are not part of the fifty obligatory rak'ahs; rather, they are additional voluntary rak'ahs to complete the fifty.
These extra rak'ahs serve as compensation, with two voluntary rak'ahs taking the place of every rak'ah of obligation.

The traveler and the sick are permitted to perform the night prayer at the beginning of the night due to their preoccupation, weakness, or to ensure they fulfil their prayers and gain rest or focus on their travel."
